title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative Result under Shared‑Generation Semantics
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether a deterministic verifier pipeline (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals from a hosted LLM on synthetic NetOps tasks. Design: N=200 deterministic intent→configuration tasks in a paired design comparing (a) baseline LLM-only and (b) guarded pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one LLM call per task) producing model_calls_used = 200 (preregistered independent per-arm generation would have used up to 400). Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Because identical per-pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that the deterministic verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this execution. We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of this testability failure, and give concrete, artifact‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, exploratory ROC reserves) for informative repeats. All execution and analysis artifacts cited here are archived in the supplied bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating human‑intent → device‑configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) is a rapidly growing NetOps research direction because it can reduce operator effort and accelerate maintenance. Incorrectly specified or misordered changes, however, can produce outages, violate policies, or introduce security exposures. A widely advocated mitigation is tool‑augmentation: pair an LLM generator with deterministic validators, sandboxed simulators, or constrained executors in a generate–validate–repair pipeline so that proposed changes are checked before execution.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) to quantify whether a deterministic verifier reduces verifier‑detected unsafe proposals from a hosted LLM under benign and adversarial prompt clusters. The primary estimand was the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) on binary validator outcomes, tested with an exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap CIs (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistered design specified N=200 paired tasks, a deterministic topology/task generator, and two permitted generation semantics: independent per‑arm generation or shared_initial_candidate (one shared LLM call per task). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate to conserve model‑call budget.

Key outcome and framing: the run produced a ceiling (concordant) outcome—every confirmatory episode was labeled SAFE by the deterministic validator for both arms (baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200). This ceiling produced an estimated paired difference of 0.0, p = 1.0 and a degenerate CI [0.0,0.0]. Critically, this is a testability/failure‑of‑design result—not evidence that the LLM+validator pipeline is safe in production. Our contribution is artifact‑centred: (1) publish a complete, deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts; (2) give a precise, artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory test was non‑informative under the executed semantics; and (3) provide concrete, archive‑supported design recommendations to make repeats informative.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and prototype reports document rapid interest in applying LLMs to NetOps (intent translation, configuration synthesis, diagnosis and limited remediation) and highlight both promise and safety concerns where models produce executable changes [https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12729; https://openalex.org/W7161354925; https://openalex.org/W7170714602]. The literature repeatedly advocates tool‑augmentation (generate–validate–repair or divide–verify–refine pipelines) and shows empirical gains in constrained settings when the external verifier faithfully encodes domain constraints [https://openalex.org/W4412888330; https://openalex.org/W7161354925].

At the same time, prior work emphasizes methodological sensitivity: measured improvements depend on verifier fidelity, sampling semantics (how candidate generations are drawn and whether repairs are applied), and evaluation workflows (sandboxed replay, explicit initial/final states). Guardrail and agent orchestration literature warn about operational trade‑offs: stricter validators can reduce unsafe acceptances but increase false refusals and operator burden unless calibrated with adversarial testing and ROC‑style diagnostics [https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.177006109.97957916/v1; https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1].

Our experiment aligns with these threads by preregistering a paired estimand, using a deterministic task generator and sandboxed validator, and archiving full validator traces and execution manifests so runs are replayable. The observed non‑informative outcome illustrates the evaluation‑semantic sensitivity highlighted across the cited works and reinforces the practical need for generation budgeting and adversarial calibration in confirmatory NetOps experiments.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as cand-2026-01-prereg-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline measured on binary SAFE indicators from deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration specified N=200 paired tasks, planned paired episodes = 400, and a power design that targeted detecting ≈7 percentage‑point paired reductions assuming baseline unsafe ≈10–15%.

Task generator, scope, and seeds. A deterministic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks constrained to single‑AS multi‑device topologies and limited fields (admin, mtu, vlan). The preregistration fixed generator RNG behavior (seeding conventions and per‑task generation_seed values); the manifest records per‑task generation_seed entries and full task_payloads. Tasks included explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, and required_sequence constraints so the validator could perform deterministic full_intent_constraint_validation.

Compared pipelines and generation semantics. Baseline: post‑hoc scoring of the LLM candidate (no runtime enforcement). Guarded: deterministic sandbox validation of the same candidate using deterministic_netops_validator_v5; repairs were instrumented in the harness but repair_provider_trace fields for confirmatory episodes are null (no repairs invoked). The preregistration allowed two generation semantics: independent per‑arm generation (two model calls per task) or shared_initial_candidate (one LLM call per task, shared by both arms). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false) to conserve hosted model budget; this choice is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json.

Scoring and analysis. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 emitted deterministic 'valid' flags and violation lists under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Confirmatory binary outcomes were derived from validator.valid (1 = SAFE, 0 = UNSAFE). Analysis was performed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 yielding the 2×2 contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), exact McNemar p‑value, and paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Missingness, exclusion, and retry rules from the preregistration were applied; the run recorded no technical failures or exclusions.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and manifested resources. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes), failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200 (execution/execution_manifest.json). The executed model configuration declares requested_model = gpt-5-mini and independent_condition_generation = false (execution/model_configuration.json), matching the shared_initial_candidate semantics. Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200, and no cross‑condition cache reuse; deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The deterministic validator produced SAFE labels for every confirmatory episode: baseline SAFE = 200/200 and guarded SAFE = 200/200. Contingency counts are n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). From these counts the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test computed p = 1.0; the paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI is degenerate at [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These numerical outputs are direct archival analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).

Representative diagnostic evidence. Representative scoring JSONs and shared response files show identical generated candidates across baseline and guarded episodes for many tasks; validator traces (validation_before/after) show violation_count = 0 and valid = true in all confirmatory scoring JSONs, and repair_provider_trace entries are null—confirming that no repair mechanism produced discordant guarded candidates. The analysis/missingness_summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes; analysis/contamination_summary lists no flagged items.

Statistical interpretation. McNemar’s test and paired bootstrap CI rely on discordant pairs (n10 and n01). The observed absence of discordant pairs (n10 = n01 = 0) renders the preregistered inferential machinery non‑informative for the intended causal estimand: the arms had no opportunity to disagree because they scored identical candidates and no repairs or nondeterministic validator outcomes occurred. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline unsafe rate (~10–15%) and discordant proportions; those assumptions were not met because of the executed generation semantics and the sampled model behavior.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded diagnosis of testability failure. Three archived facts jointly explain the inferential degeneracy: (1) executed generation semantics: independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate) produced a single LLM candidate per task that both arms scored (execution/model_configuration.json; execution/execution_manifest.json); (2) validator verdicts: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every sampled candidate as valid (analysis/condition_summary.csv; execution/scoring/*.json); and (3) absence of repair‑driven discordance: repair_provider_trace fields are null across confirmatory scoring JSONs, so the guarded pipeline did not alter candidates. Because these facts are recorded in the archived manifests and scoring JSONs, they deterministically explain why no discordant pairs were observed.

Design implications and artifact‑supported recommendations. The archival manifests make the resource trade‑offs explicit. Independent per‑arm generation was preregistered as the design that would permit a direct paired causal contrast; it would have required roughly 200 additional model calls (planned maximum_model_calls = 400 vs executed model_calls_used = 200). To enable an informative repeat we recommend (all preregistration‑aligned): (a) adopt independent per‑arm generation for confirmatory paired contrasts unless the guarded arm will deterministically repair candidates in a way that can produce discordance; (b) consume the preregistered exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) to calibrate adversarial transform parameters until the baseline unsafe rate matches the power assumptions; (c) instrument and archive repair_provider_trace when repairs are permitted and quantify UNSAFE→SAFE conversions; and (d) run a deterministic pilot holdout to detect ceiling/floor contingencies and invoke preregistered contingency‑preserving actions (e.g., flip to independent draws) before committing to the full confirmatory set. Each recommendation maps directly to artifacts and fields in the preregistration and execution manifests.

Alternative estimands under constrained budgets. When independent per‑arm draws are infeasible, consider estimands testable under shared semantics: (i) absolute LLM unsafe‑proposal rate (single‑arm proportion with CIs); (ii) guarded refusal and post‑repair SAFE rates (requires repairs and repair traces); or (iii) exploratory ROC estimation using injected ground‑truth unsafe cases. The preregistration already listed several secondary_estimands and exploratory items that map to these options; selecting one of them preserves inferential validity under constrained budgets.

Threats to validity and operational caution. The validator ran deterministically against synthetic, single‑AS tasks restricted to admin/mtu/vlan fields; thus zero unsafe detections here do not imply production safety. The archived limitations (section below) enumerate construct and external‑validity threats (synthetic scope, single model, validator completeness, absence of operator workload measurement). Operators should not extrapolate safety from this run without wider validator validation and adversarial stress tests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived preregistered paired experiment comparing gpt-5-mini baseline generation and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics the sampled LLM outputs were labeled SAFE in every confirmatory episode (paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and because the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis was not testable in this run. The scientific contribution is therefore methodological and reproducibility‑centred: (1) a complete deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts that permit exact replay; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative for verifier efficacy; and (3) concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, exploratory ROC estimation, and pilot contingency checks) for informative repeats. Practitioners seeking to evaluate verifier efficacy should budget per‑arm generation or instrument repair paths and use exploratory calibration so confirmatory estimands remain testable. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced above are archived in the supplied bundle and permit deterministic replication of the diagnosis and outputs.

limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt-5-mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
